A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VisReason and VisReason-Pro work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark and grounding results, dataset/zoom ablations, and a blinded human evaluation in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds inference-format comparisons, second-backbone experiments, source-removal results, an annotation audit and evaluator calibration.

M1.justification: The dataset-generation algorithms, autoregressive LoRA fine-tuning objective and adaptive zoom-and-verify procedure remain unchanged. The additional backbone and inference-format experiments do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 489K/165K resources, the same eleven source datasets across four domains, and MME/V* evaluation. The new audits, prompt comparisons and source-removal ablation operate within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The main Visual-CoT and grounding comparator sets remain unchanged. However, v1 Table 5's external-benchmark comparison is replaced by v2 Table 7, which adds Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL-based trained variants while removing MiniGPTv2, VisCoT-7B and LLaVA-NeXT from that comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds matched direct-QA tests of fixed checkpoints, one-epoch InternVL training, source-removal experiments and a stratified 2,200-example audit. It revises the appendix learning rate from 1e-5 to 2e-5 and changes the main-text ViT setting to frozen, matching v1's appendix. Table 2 newly specifies sample-weighted averages, although Appendix C still says macro-averaging. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained dataset/zoom ablations and user study, v2 adds substantial analyses of output-format sensitivity, backbone transfer, dependence on training sources, annotation quality and automatic-judge validity (Tables 3, 6, 7 and 12-16). These test important questions that v1 did not empirically address.

E5.justification: v1 mainly reports point estimates. v2 newly reports five judge evaluations per example, Wilson 95% confidence intervals for the annotation audit, and confidence intervals for evaluator scores, correlations, weighted kappa and agreement. The five-pass disclosure does not establish an increase over a known v1 run count; additional training seeds are not reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains per-dataset scores but revises several averages, including VisReason-Pro from 0.807 to 0.802 and VisCoT-7B from 0.580 to 0.614; ablation values also change. Substantial new results cover direct-QA inference, InternVL transfer, source removal, annotation quality and judge calibration. For example, newly reported VisReason-Pro direct-QA scores are 0.856 on MME and 0.791 on V*, under a different inference protocol from the retained multi-round results.

T1.justification: The probabilistic formulation, training loss, coordinate operations and grounding-metric definitions are retained. Neither version introduces new theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations relative to the other.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes broad cross-benchmark generalization, robustness and 3D grounding. v2 narrows the abstract and conclusion toward fine-grained/spatial improvements and ordinal-depth/RoI evaluation, while adding claims of transfer across backbones. This materially changes the claimed scope, although the dataset and core resource contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the earlier cropping-based explanation of Doc/Text degradation with evidence supporting inference-format mismatch. It newly discusses source-dependent gains, mixed backbone transfer, weaker document rationales, noisy nonmetric depth, inference latency and cascading localization failures without backtracking. These substantially qualify applicability and explain failure mechanisms.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page URL, identifies GPT-4o-mini as the evaluator, specifies score-field parsing and malformed-output handling, and adds dropout/DDP details. Training-setting documentation is revised. Most hardware, LoRA, image/token budgets and generation prompts were already supplied in v1; the PDFs do not establish availability of the linked resources.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussions and citations for VGR, Zebra-CoT, CodePlot-CoT and other works, while removing the LLaVA-Plus citation. Positioning becomes more qualified around scale, multi-round RoI supervision and ordinal-depth coverage, but retains the existing model-oriented/dataset-oriented framework. Bibliographic updates and duplicate consolidation are presentation changes.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, contribution statements, related-work discussion, experimental interpretation and conclusion. It introduces dedicated error-analysis, transfer and limitations discussions and reorganizes the appendix into lettered sections with a substantial additional-results section.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout with running headers. Table 2 becomes stacked panels, the external comparison is redesigned, and new format-analysis, transfer, audit and calibration tables are inserted. Figure 6 gains a bird comparison; most existing pipeline, prompt and appendix-example figures are retained and resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The 2,200-example annotation audit and human calibration of the evaluator address important validation gaps in v1's automatically generated dataset and scoring pipeline. Matched inference-format tests and transfer/source-removal analyses also support substantially better-bounded claims and clearer limitations. These gains improve the paper's evidential credibility rather than merely increasing reported performance. Residual problems, especially the conflicting weighted-versus-macro averaging descriptions, limit reproducibility but do not outweigh the added validation and more careful interpretation.
